operators.name: AgentOperator
operators.description: Run a pydantic-ai Agent with tools and multi-turn reasoning.

params.name: prompt
params.description: The prompt to send to the agent.

params.name: llm_conn_id
params.description: Connection ID for the LLM provider.

params.name: model_id
params.description: Model identifier (e.g. `"openai:gpt-5"`). Overrides the model stored in the connection's extra field.

params.name: fallback_conn_ids
params.description: Connection IDs to fail over to, in order, when the primary provider is unavailable. Overrides the `fallback_conn_ids` set in the connection's extra field. `None` (default) reads the connection's own extra field; an explicit `[]` disables a chain configured there. See airflow.providers.common.ai.hooks.pydantic_ai.PydanticAIHook for how blank entries in the list are dropped.

params.name: system_prompt
params.description: System-level instructions for the agent.

params.name: enable_tool_logging
params.description: When `True` (default), the operator appends a `ToolLoggingCapability`, whose `get_wrapper_toolset` wraps the agent's assembled function toolset so that tool calls are logged with timing at INFO level and arguments at DEBUG level. If `capabilities` already holds a `ToolLoggingCapability`, the operator adds none and that one's `logger` is used. Logging includes tools supplied through `toolsets=`, `agent_params["tools"]`, and capabilities, but not output tools, provider-native tools that run server-side, or tools another capability adds through its own wrapper (code mode's `run_code`, ToolSearch's `search_tools`). Set to `False` to disable.

params.name: agent_params
params.description: Additional keyword arguments passed to the pydantic-ai `Agent` constructor (e.g. `retries`, `model_settings`).

params.name: usage_limits
params.description: Optional pydantic-ai pydantic_ai.usage.UsageLimits enforced on every agent run (initial run, durable replay, and HITL regeneration), or a dict of the same fields (e.g. `{"cost_limit": "{{ params.budget }}", "request_limit": 5}`). The dict form is templated: each value is rendered by Jinja like any other `template_fields` entry, then coerced to that field's type (`Decimal`, `int`, or `bool`). A value that cannot be coerced -- a Variable that exists but is empty renders to `""`, a typo renders to a non-numeric string -- fails the task with a `ValueError` naming the field and the rendered value, instead of silently disabling the limit. A `UsageLimits` instance passed directly is used as-is and is not templated or validated. `None` (default) sets no token, cost, or tool-call limits, but pydantic-ai still caps each run at its default `request_limit` of `50` requests.

params.name: durable
params.description: When `True`, attaches airflow.providers.common.ai.durable.AirflowDurability, which records each step the agent completes -- model responses, tool calls from any toolset or capability, tool discovery, and other capabilities' `@durable_operation` methods -- in a journal kept for the task instance. On retry the agent runs again from the start and the steps the previous attempt completed are replayed from the journal instead of running again. Each step is replayed only if it matches what the previous attempt did at the same point: if the prompt, model, settings, tools, tool arguments or message history changed, that step and every step after it run live (with a warning). Default `False`. A replayed step adds nothing to the usage counted against `usage_limits` or reported in the `usage` XCom -- not its request, tokens, cost, or tool calls -- so every attempt counts only the model and tool calls it actually makes. Clearing a finished task instance starts a fresh budget; whether its rerun replays from the journal depends on the Airflow version and how the task was cleared (durable-clear). The agent's `run_id` (and its `conversation_id`, when there is no message history) stays the first attempt's on every retry. On Airflow >= 3.3 the journal is kept in the AIP-103 task state store, so no extra configuration is needed. On older Airflow versions it is persisted to ObjectStorage and requires `[common.ai] durable_cache_path` to be set. A pydantic-ai `MCPToolset` needs a unique `id`, and so do capabilities with `@durable_operation` methods. A `FunctionToolset` or a function that builds a toolset, passed in `toolsets` or `agent_params["toolsets"]`, needs none, and neither does a `FunctionToolset` held directly by a `Toolset` capability (durable-toolset-ids). A tool with the metadata `{"airflow": False}` runs again on every attempt instead of replaying (durable-tool-opt-out). Cannot be combined with a `SandboxToolset` (raises), attached or not: a replayed tool result describes a workspace state the replay did not reproduce, and the first call that misses the cache runs against whatever the sandbox holds now. With a pydantic-ai-harness `CodeMode` capability, a retry runs each `run_code` snippet again and replays the tool calls it makes; `CodeMode`'s `eager` and `speculate` options are off while the run is durable.

params.name: cache_prompt
params.description: When `True` (default), asks the provider to cache the tool definitions, system prompt and conversation so far, so the next request in the run -- and a mapped task's other instances within the cache lifetime -- reads them back at a fraction of the input price instead of paying for them again. Turns on prompt caching for Anthropic models and for Bedrock and OpenRouter models that support it; a no-op for OpenAI and Gemini, which cache long prompts on their own. A provider's own cache settings in `agent_params["model_settings"]` or a spec file take precedence: setting any `anthropic_cache*` key leaves Anthropic caching entirely to you, and a `CachePoint` in the prompt or message history leaves all of it to you. Set `False` where a cache write is rarely read back, such as a single long request that is not mapped. See agent-prompt-caching for when caching costs more than it saves.

params.name: message_history
params.description: Prior conversation to seed the run with, for multi-turn sessions that span task runs. Accepts a `list` of pydantic-ai `ModelMessage` objects, or their JSON form as `str` / `bytes` -- e.g. `"{{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='ask', key='message_history', default='[]') }}"` (pass `default='[]'` so the first run, with no XCom yet, starts a fresh session instead of failing to parse the string `"None"`). `None` (default) is a single-turn run -- no behavior change. When set (an empty `[]` / `""` starts a fresh session), the full transcript after the run -- `result.all_messages()` -- is pushed to XCom under the key `message_history` so the next run can resume. Persisting that transcript under a session key (e.g. in object storage) is the DAG's responsibility. The transcript is cumulative and grows each turn; for long sessions use an object-storage XCom backend or trim old turns. Not supported together with `enable_hitl_review` (raises) -- the post-review transcript is not yet recoverable.

params.name: emit_message_history
params.description: Push the post-run transcript to XCom under the key `message_history`. Defaults to `True` when `message_history` is set and `False` otherwise. Set `True` to record a single-turn run without seeding it, or `False` to keep a seeded run from pushing it. Not supported together with `enable_hitl_review` (raises).

params.name: enable_hitl_review
params.description: When `True`, the operator enters an iterative review loop after the first generation. A human reviewer can approve, reject, or request changes via the plugin's REST API at `/hitl-review` or through the **HITL Review** extra link on the task instance. Default `False`. Cannot be combined with a `SandboxToolset` that provisions its own sandbox (raises): regeneration after feedback is a second run, which would start from an empty sandbox while its history describes the first run's files. A `SandboxToolset` attached to a sandbox another task owns (`attach_to`) is fine, since both runs find the same files, as long as the reviewer answers inside that sandbox's lifetime: the wait spends the provisioning backend's `sandbox_timeout`.

params.name: max_hitl_iterations
params.description: Maximum outputs shown to the reviewer (1 = initial output). When the reviewer requests changes at iteration >= this limit, the task fails with `HITLMaxIterationsError` without calling the LLM. E.g. 5 allows changes at iterations 1–4. Default `5`.

params.name: hitl_timeout
params.description: Maximum wall-clock time to wait for all review rounds combined. `None` means no wall-clock timeout; the review still ends on a terminal action (approve or reject), `max_hitl_iterations`, or when polling the human action XCom fails too many times in a row.

params.name: hitl_poll_interval
params.description: Seconds between XCom polls while waiting for a human response. Default `10`.

params.name: serialize_output
params.description: If `True`, an output that is itself a Pydantic `BaseModel` is dumped with `model_dump()` before being pushed to XCom, so `date` and `Decimal` fields keep their types. Default `False`: a model whose class the worker registers from `output_type` flows through XCom unchanged. Some outputs are pushed as dicts either way; see When a model arrives as a dict.

params.name: tool_approval_timeout
params.description: How long the pause waits for a decision. `None` (default) waits indefinitely. Must be positive.

params.name: on_tool_approval_timeout
params.description: What a timed-out pause does: `"fail"` (default) fails the task, `"deny"` rejects the pending calls so the agent carries on without them, and needs a `tool_approval_timeout`. There is no approve-on-timeout.

params.name: tool_approval_assigned_users
params.description: Users allowed to decide. `None` (default) leaves it to anyone who can act on the task's Required Actions.

operators.name: DocumentLoaderOperator
operators.description: Parse files into `list[dict(text, metadata)]` for downstream embedding.

params.name: source_path
params.description: A local path, glob pattern, or storage URI (`s3://`, `gs://`, `azure://`, `file://`, ...). Cloud URIs go through airflow.sdk.ObjectStoragePath / fsspec. `**` enables recursive matching, for both local paths and cloud URIs. Wildcards must not appear in the scheme or bucket segment of a cloud URI.

params.name: source_conn_id
params.description: Airflow connection ID used by `ObjectStoragePath` for cloud URIs (`aws_default`, `google_cloud_default`, ...). Ignored for local paths.

params.name: file_type
params.description: File extension hint (e.g. `".pdf"`). Required when using `source_bytes`, since bytes carry no extension to detect. Omitting it is rejected when the operator is constructed -- Dag parse time for a regular task, run time for a mapped one, since `expand()` validates argument names only and defers construction to `unmap()`. Optional with `source_path`, where it overrides auto-detection.

params.name: parser
params.description: Parsing backend selection. `"auto"` (default) picks the backend from the file extension.

params.name: file_extensions
params.description: When `source_path` is a directory or glob, only process files whose extension is in this list. When omitted, the operator processes only files whose extension is known to the built-in dispatch (others are skipped with a warning) and silently ignores files whose name starts with a dot.

params.name: metadata_fields
params.description: Extra key-value pairs merged into every document's `metadata` dict. Auto-extracted fields such as `file_name`, `file_path`, `row_index`, `item_index`, and `page_number` take precedence over keys with the same name.

params.name: encoding
params.description: Text encoding used for `.txt`/`.md`/`.csv`/`.json`/`.jsonl` and for the bytes path. Defaults to `"utf-8"`.

params.name: encoding_errors
params.description: How decode errors are handled. Defaults to `"strict"`; set to `"replace"` or `"ignore"` to tolerate mixed-encoding inputs at the cost of some character loss.

params.name: json_text_field
params.description: When parsing JSON or JSON Lines, treat this key as the embedding text and put every other key into `metadata`. Applies to each item when the top-level JSON is a list, to the object when it is a single dict, or to each JSON Lines record. When `None` (default), the operator flattens dicts into `"k: v, k: v"` text (same shape as the CSV parser).

operators.name: LlamaIndexEmbeddingOperator
operators.description: Chunk documents and produce embedding vectors using LlamaIndex.

params.name: documents
params.description: List of dicts with `text` and `metadata` keys, typically from `DocumentLoaderOperator` or a `@task`. Templated, so binding via `my_loader.output` (XCom direct) resolves to the native `list[dict]` before `execute` runs.

params.name: llm_conn_id
params.description: Airflow connection ID for the embedding API. Falls back to LlamaIndexHook.default_conn_name when `None`.

params.name: embed_conn_id
params.description: Optional separate Airflow connection ID for the embedding provider. Falls back to `llm_conn_id` when `None`.

params.name: embedding_kwargs
params.description: Additional keyword arguments passed to the embedding model constructor without filtering when `embed_model` is a string or omitted. Nested options supported by the underlying library can override hook-provided request values, including credentials, the model, and the input. Only pass trusted values.

params.name: chunk_size
params.description: Chunk size for the sentence splitter.

params.name: chunk_overlap
params.description: Overlap between chunks.

params.name: persist_dir
params.description: Optional path to persist the index. Accepts local paths and storage URIs (`s3://`, `gs://`, ...) resolved via airflow.sdk.ObjectStoragePath.

params.name: persist_conn_id
params.description: Airflow connection ID for cloud-storage credentials when `persist_dir` is a URI.

operators.name: LlamaIndexRetrievalOperator
operators.description: Retrieve relevant document chunks from a persisted LlamaIndex index.

params.name: query
params.description: The query string. Supports Jinja templating.

params.name: index_persist_dir
params.description: Local path or storage URI (`s3://`, `gs://`, ...) pointing at the persisted LlamaIndex index. Resolved via airflow.sdk.ObjectStoragePath when a URI scheme is present.

params.name: persist_conn_id
params.description: Airflow connection ID for cloud-storage credentials when `index_persist_dir` is a URI.

params.name: llm_conn_id
params.description: Airflow connection ID for the embedding API. Falls back to LlamaIndexHook.default_conn_name when `None`. Used only when `embed_model` is a string (or omitted entirely).

params.name: embed_conn_id
params.description: Optional separate Airflow connection ID for the embedding provider. Falls back to `llm_conn_id` when `None`.

params.name: embedding_kwargs
params.description: Additional keyword arguments passed to the embedding model constructor without filtering when `embed_model` is a string or omitted. Options that affect vector dimensions must match those used to build the index. Nested options supported by the underlying library can override hook-provided request values, including credentials, the model, and the input. Only pass trusted values.

params.name: top_k
params.description: Number of top results to retrieve.

operators.name: LLMOperator
operators.description: Call an LLM with a prompt and return the output.

params.name: prompt
params.description: The prompt to send to the LLM.

params.name: llm_conn_id
params.description: Connection ID for the LLM provider.

params.name: model_id
params.description: Model identifier (e.g. `"openai:gpt-5"`). Overrides the model stored in the connection's extra field.

params.name: fallback_conn_ids
params.description: Connection IDs to fail over to, in order, when the primary provider is unavailable. Overrides the `fallback_conn_ids` set in the connection's extra field. `None` (default) reads the connection's own extra field; an explicit `[]` disables a chain configured there. See airflow.providers.common.ai.hooks.pydantic_ai.PydanticAIHook for how blank entries in the list are dropped.

params.name: system_prompt
params.description: System-level instructions for the LLM agent.

params.name: model_settings
params.description: Pydantic AI pydantic_ai.settings.ModelSettings for the model call, such as `temperature` or `max_tokens`, including provider-specific settings. `None` (default) uses the model's defaults.

params.name: output_retries
params.description: How many times the model is asked again when its output fails validation against `output_type`. `None` (default) uses Pydantic AI's default.

params.name: usage_limits
params.description: Optional pydantic-ai pydantic_ai.usage.UsageLimits enforced on the run, or a dict of the same fields (e.g. `{"cost_limit": "{{ params.budget }}", "request_limit": 5}`). The dict form is templated: each value is rendered by Jinja like any other `template_fields` entry, then coerced to that field's type (`Decimal`, `int`, or `bool`). A value that cannot be coerced -- a Variable that exists but is empty renders to `""`, a typo renders to a non-numeric string -- fails the task with a `ValueError` naming the field and the rendered value, instead of silently disabling the limit. A `UsageLimits` instance passed directly is used as-is and is not templated or validated. `None` (default) sets no token, cost, or tool-call limits, but pydantic-ai still caps the run at its default `request_limit` of `50` requests.

params.name: require_approval
params.description: If `True`, the task pauses after generating output (`awaiting_input` on Airflow 3.3+, deferred on 3.1 and 3.2) and waits for a human reviewer to approve or reject via the HITL interface. Default `False`. Needs Airflow 3.1+.

params.name: approval_timeout
params.description: Maximum time to wait for a review. When exceeded, `on_approval_timeout` decides the outcome.

params.name: on_approval_timeout
params.description: What to do when `approval_timeout` expires without a review. `"fail"` (default) fails the task with `HITLTimeoutError`; `"approve"` and `"reject"` answer the review with that option, so the task resumes as if a reviewer had chosen it. The chosen option is also pre-highlighted for the reviewer in the HITL form. Requires a review path (`require_approval=True` or a `decision_policy` that reviews) and a positive `approval_timeout`.

params.name: allow_modifications
params.description: If `True`, the reviewer can edit the output before approving. The edit is converted back into `output_type` and returned as the task result. For a type pydantic can validate, an edit that does not validate fails the task with `ReviewedOutputValidationError`; a retry runs the model again. Default `False`.

params.name: approval_assigned_users
params.description: Users allowed to answer the review, as `{"id": ..., "name": ...}` dicts where `id` is the auth manager's user id. `None` (default) lets any user with the permission respond. On Airflow 3.1 to 3.3 the list is fixed when the review is first created; on 3.4+ a cleared or retried task replaces it. Needs Airflow 3.1+.

params.name: fail_on_reject
params.description: If `False`, a rejected review skips the direct downstream tasks except teardowns and the task succeeds, as airflow.providers.standard.operators.hitl.ApprovalOperator does. Only takes effect when a review is opened. Default `True`: a rejection fails the task.

params.name: ignore_downstream_trigger_rules
params.description: If `True`, a rejected review that does not fail the task skips every downstream task except teardowns rather than only the direct ones. Only takes effect when a review is opened. Default `False`.

params.name: serialize_output
params.description: If `True`, an output that is itself a Pydantic `BaseModel` is dumped with `model_dump()` before being pushed to XCom, so `date` and `Decimal` fields keep their types. Default `False`: a model whose class the worker registers from `output_type` flows through XCom unchanged. Some outputs are pushed as dicts either way; see When a model arrives as a dict.

operators.name: LLMBatchOperator
operators.description: Submit prompts as a provider batch job and land results on object storage.

params.name: requests
params.description: The batch's inputs: a list of prompt strings, or a list of dicts with a `"prompt"` key and optional `model`, `system_prompt`, `max_tokens` and `params` overrides.

params.name: result_path
params.description: Directory URI (not a file path) where the JSONL results and internal state are written, e.g. `s3://bucket/prefix`. Templated, but must render to the same value on every attempt of a task instance; a retry looks for its recorded state there.

params.name: llm_conn_id
params.description: Connection ID for the LLM provider. Must be a `pydanticai` connection today.

params.name: model_id
params.description: Model identifier as `"<provider>:<model>"` (e.g. `"openai:gpt-5"`). Falls back to the connection's Model field, as `LLMOperator` does. A bare name takes the connection's Default Provider, and `openai-chat:` selects the OpenAI adapter.

params.name: system_prompt
params.description: System-level instructions applied to every request that does not set its own `system_prompt` override.

params.name: max_tokens
params.description: Output token cap for requests that do not set their own. Sent as `max_tokens` to Anthropic and as `max_completion_tokens` to OpenAI.

params.name: request_params
params.description: Extra body parameters merged into every request (e.g. `{"temperature": 0.2}`); a request's own `params` wins on conflicting keys. The keys the operator manages (`model`, the messages, the token cap and the structured-output directive) cannot be overridden from here. Templated: every string inside the dict is rendered, and Jinja hands back a string, so a numeric parameter written as a template needs `render_template_as_native_obj=True` on the Dag.

params.name: poll_interval
params.description: Seconds between status checks. Minimum 30.

params.name: timeout
params.description: Seconds to wait for the batch to reach a terminal state, measured from submission. Default 24 hours. When a retry re-attaches to a batch whose budget has already elapsed (`cancel_on_timeout=False`), it gets a fresh `timeout` measured from the retry. If `execution_timeout` is set below `timeout + poll_interval + 60`, Airflow's hard timeout preempts this graceful path and `cancel_on_timeout` never runs.

params.name: deferrable
params.description: Run in deferrable mode. Defaults to `[operators] default_deferrable`.

params.name: cancel_on_kill
params.description: Cancel the batch when the task is killed. In deferrable mode this runs from the trigger's `on_kill`, which only Airflow 3.3+ calls; there, clearing or marking a deferred task from the UI counts as a kill.

params.name: cancel_on_timeout
params.description: Cancel the batch when `timeout` is reached without a terminal state. When `False`, the task still fails, but the batch keeps running (and billing) and a later retry re-attaches to it.

params.name: fail_on_partial_error
params.description: Fail the task when any request errored on the provider side, failed output validation, expired, was cancelled, or is missing from the results. Default `False`: the task succeeds and the manifest's `counts` records each bucket. A batch in which every request failed still counts as partial.

params.name: on_stale_state
params.description: What to do when a recorded batch for this task instance no longer matches the current input (prompts, model, `output_type` schema, ...): `"cancel_and_resubmit"` (default) best-effort cancels the stale batch and submits a new one; `"fail"` raises instead.

params.name: on_orphaned_intent
params.description: What to do when a previous attempt recorded its intent to submit but no batch id, and the provider-side lookup finds no matching batch: `"resubmit"` (default) submits a new batch; `"fail"` raises instead. Anthropic offers no such lookup, so `"resubmit"` may pay twice there if the original request did reach the provider.

params.name: completion_window
params.description: OpenAI-specific completion window. Only `"24h"` is offered by the API today. Ignored by Anthropic.

operators.name: LLMBranchOperator
operators.description: Ask an LLM to choose which downstream task(s) to execute.

params.name: branches
params.description: Optional mapping of downstream task ID to a BranchOption, or to a string as shorthand for its description. The description travels in the output schema next to the option, so the model reads "here is an option, here is what it means" rather than guessing from the task ID; `min_confidence` on an option, which is experimental, is a bar for that branch alone. A downstream task without an entry is presented by its ID alone and takes the policy's bar; some decision-model servers refuse an option without a description, so describe every branch when the connection is a decision model. A key that is not a downstream task ID fails the task before the model is called. Descriptions support Jinja templating.

params.name: allow_multiple_branches
params.description: When `False` (default) the LLM returns a single task ID. When `True` the LLM may return one or more task IDs.

params.name: fail_on_reject
params.description: If `True`, a rejected review fails the task instead of skipping the downstream tasks. Generally discouraged, as for airflow.providers.standard.operators.hitl.ApprovalOperator. Only takes effect when a review is opened. Default `False`, unlike airflow.providers.common.ai.operators.llm.LLMOperator.

operators.name: LLMFileAnalysisOperator
operators.description: Analyze files from object storage or local storage using a single LLM call.

params.name: file_path
params.description: File or prefix to analyze.

params.name: file_conn_id
params.description: Optional connection ID for the storage backend. Overrides a connection embedded in `file_path`.

params.name: multi_modal
params.description: Allow PNG/JPG/PDF inputs as binary attachments. Default `False`.

params.name: max_files
params.description: Maximum number of files to include from a prefix. Excess files are omitted and noted in the prompt. Default `20`.

params.name: max_file_size_bytes
params.description: Maximum size of any single input file. Default `5 MiB`.

params.name: max_total_size_bytes
params.description: Maximum cumulative size across all resolved files. Default `20 MiB`.

params.name: max_text_chars
params.description: Maximum normalized text context passed to the LLM after sampling/truncation. Default `100000`.

params.name: sample_rows
params.description: Maximum number of sampled rows or records included for CSV, Parquet, and Avro inputs. This limits structural preview depth, while `max_file_size_bytes` and `max_total_size_bytes` limit bytes read from storage and `max_text_chars` limits the final prompt text budget. Default `10`.

params.name: prompt
params.description: The analysis prompt for the LLM.

params.name: llm_conn_id
params.description: Connection ID for the LLM provider.

params.name: model_id
params.description: Model identifier (e.g. `"openai:gpt-5"`). Overrides the model stored in the connection's extra field.

params.name: fallback_conn_ids
params.description: Connection IDs to fail over to, in order, when the primary provider is unavailable. Overrides the `fallback_conn_ids` set in the connection's extra field. `None` (default) reads the connection's own extra field; an explicit `[]` disables a chain configured there. See airflow.providers.common.ai.hooks.pydantic_ai.PydanticAIHook for how blank entries in the list are dropped.

params.name: system_prompt
params.description: Additional instructions appended to the built-in file-analysis system prompt.

params.name: model_settings
params.description: Pydantic AI `ModelSettings` for the model call, such as `temperature` or `max_tokens`. See airflow.providers.common.ai.operators.llm.LLMOperator.

params.name: output_retries
params.description: How many times the model is asked again when its output fails validation. See airflow.providers.common.ai.operators.llm.LLMOperator.

params.name: usage_limits
params.description: Optional pydantic-ai pydantic_ai.usage.UsageLimits enforced on the run, or a dict of the same fields (e.g. `{"cost_limit": "{{ params.budget }}", "request_limit": 5}`). The dict form is templated: each value is rendered by Jinja like any other `template_fields` entry, then coerced to that field's type (`Decimal`, `int`, or `bool`). A value that cannot be coerced -- a Variable that exists but is empty renders to `""`, a typo renders to a non-numeric string -- fails the task with a `ValueError` naming the field and the rendered value, instead of silently disabling the limit. A `UsageLimits` instance passed directly is used as-is and is not templated or validated. `None` (default) sets no token, cost, or tool-call limits, but pydantic-ai still caps the run at its default `request_limit` of `50` requests.

params.name: require_approval
params.description: If `True`, the task pauses after generating output (`awaiting_input` on Airflow 3.3+, deferred on 3.1 and 3.2) and waits for a human reviewer to approve or reject via the HITL interface. Default `False`. Needs Airflow 3.1+.

params.name: approval_timeout
params.description: Maximum time to wait for a review. When exceeded, `on_approval_timeout` decides the outcome.

params.name: on_approval_timeout
params.description: What to do when `approval_timeout` expires without a review. `"fail"` (default) fails the task with `HITLTimeoutError`; `"approve"` and `"reject"` answer the review with that option, so the task resumes as if a reviewer had chosen it. The chosen option is also pre-highlighted for the reviewer in the HITL form. Requires a review path (`require_approval=True` or a `decision_policy` that reviews) and a positive `approval_timeout`.

params.name: allow_modifications
params.description: If `True`, the reviewer can edit the output before approving. The edit is converted back into `output_type` and returned as the task result. For a type pydantic can validate, an edit that does not validate fails the task with `ReviewedOutputValidationError`; a retry runs the model again. Default `False`.

params.name: approval_assigned_users
params.description: Users allowed to answer the review, as `{"id": ..., "name": ...}` dicts where `id` is the auth manager's user id. `None` (default) lets any user with the permission respond. On Airflow 3.1 to 3.3 the list is fixed when the review is first created; on 3.4+ a cleared or retried task replaces it. Needs Airflow 3.1+.

params.name: fail_on_reject
params.description: If `False`, a rejected review skips the direct downstream tasks except teardowns and the task succeeds, as airflow.providers.standard.operators.hitl.ApprovalOperator does. Only takes effect when a review is opened. Default `True`: a rejection fails the task.

params.name: ignore_downstream_trigger_rules
params.description: If `True`, a rejected review that does not fail the task skips every downstream task except teardowns rather than only the direct ones. Only takes effect when a review is opened. Default `False`.

params.name: serialize_output
params.description: If `True`, an output that is itself a Pydantic `BaseModel` is dumped with `model_dump()` before being pushed to XCom, so `date` and `Decimal` fields keep their types. Default `False`: a model whose class the worker registers from `output_type` flows through XCom unchanged. Some outputs are pushed as dicts either way; see When a model arrives as a dict.

operators.name: LLMSchemaCompareOperator
operators.description: Compare schemas across different database systems and detect drift using LLM reasoning.

params.name: db_conn_ids
params.description: Connection IDs for databases to compare (used with `table_names`).

params.name: table_names
params.description: Tables to introspect from each `db_conn_id`.

params.name: context_strategy
params.description: `"basic"` for column names and types only; `"full"` to include primary keys, foreign keys, and indexes. Default `"full"`.

params.name: system_prompt
params.default:
Consider cross-system type equivalences:
- varchar(n) / text / string / TEXT may be compatible
- int / integer / int4 / INT32 are equivalent
- bigint / int8 / int64 / BIGINT are equivalent
- timestamp / timestamptz / TIMESTAMP_NTZ / datetime may differ in timezone handling
- numeric(p,s) / decimal(p,s) / NUMBER — check precision and scale
- boolean / bool / BOOLEAN / tinyint(1) — check semantic equivalence

Severity levels:
- critical: Will cause data loading failures or data loss (e.g., column missing in target, incompatible types)
- warning: May cause data quality issues (e.g., precision loss, timezone mismatch)
- info: Cosmetic differences that won't affect data loading (e.g., varchar length differences within safe range)
params.description: Instructions included in the LLM system prompt. Defaults to `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` which contains cross-system type equivalences and severity definitions. Passing a value **replaces** the default system prompt

params.description: Instructions for the LLM on what to compare and flag.
